column1: # FORMULA GOLDEN - what each formula in the prover's grammar evaluates to, over its inputs.
# GENERATED by scripts/formula-golden.py from LibreOffice 24.2.7.2 and the model of scripts/formula_models.py, and Excel's own answers for the curated rows it computed; do not edit by hand.
# X <id> <home sheet> <formula> <inputs> <why it is left out>   (not part of the gate; kept so that
#   regenerating is a fixed point, and so each one can be read)
# id: <group>.<n>@<cell the formula sits in>; a corpus row's group is its corpus (sb, fuse, enron) and the
#   first 10 hex digits of the sha1 of its path relative to that corpus's root
# formula: the text of the cell's <f> element, with no leading '=' (a hostile row may hold one)
# inputs: <sheet>!<cell>=<kind>:<value>, separated by U+001F (XML 1.0 cannot hold it, so no formula and no
#   cell text can). A sheet name is quoted '...' with '' for a quote unless it is letters, digits, _ and . only.
#   kinds: n (shortest round-trip repr), b (TRUE or FALSE), s (text, as is), e (an error code). A cell not
#   listed is blank. A sheet the formula names is resolved ignoring case.
# expect: n:<shortest repr> | b:TRUE | b:FALSE | refuse
# must: 1 = a curated core row the product must answer (a refusal fails it)
# HOW A ROW IS DECIDED (gate round 8, docs/review/2026-10-02-b4-round7-spec.md, Part A). The sources, in
# order: Excel observed (requests 1, 3 and 4); Excel's own caches in the Excel-saved corpus workbooks; Microsoft's
# documentation; LibreOffice only where it agrees with Excel (HANDOFF trap 40). Request 1 is cited "Excel observed
# (16.113.3, 2026-10-02), <cell>" (docs/review/2026-10-02-excel-observations/; Sheet2 is the saved workbook's second
# sheet, extras the extras workbook); request 3 "Excel observed (request 3), <row id>"
# (docs/review/2026-10-02-excel-request-3-results/: Microsoft Excel for Mac 16.113.3, macOS 27.0.1, LOCALE en_NZ -
# decimal '.', thousands ',', currency '$' - recalculated every curated row; excel-cache.jsonl holds its outcome per
# row id, and the generator's --excel-cache reads it); request 4 "Excel observed (request 4), <row id>"
# (docs/review/2026-10-08-excel-request-4-results/formulas/, SETTLED.md: Microsoft Excel for Mac 16.113.4, macOS
# 27.0.1, region en_NZ, Excel's own separators not readable through its AppleScript on that build and no Excel
# override set, so Excel is expected to follow the region, unverified - recalculated the 94 rows of excel-probe-4;
# its excel-cache.jsonl is read beside request 3's).
# A CURATED ROW EXCEL COMPUTED holds Excel's own outcome, whatever the model or LibreOffice says:
#   excel:observed         a number (Excel's double, bit for bit) or a logical
#   error:<code>           Excel gives an error: the product must refuse
#   excel:text             Excel gives a text (an empty one included): the product caches no text, so it must refuse
#   excel:refused-on-load  Excel removed the formula on load (a literal past 9.99999999999999E+307 or underflowed,
#                          parentheses 1,000 deep): the product must refuse
#   undecided:pmt-digits   (gate round 9) a PMT-derived row whose PMT interval does not decide it (PMT below): Excel
#                          answered from its own PMT double, which no rule reproduces, so the product must refuse
#   undecided:<aspect>     (B5 gate round 3) likewise any row the model REFUSES where Excel gave a number or a logical
#                          (59 of request 4's excel-probe-4 rows; the 5 of them where Excel gives #VALUE! are
#                          error:#VALUE!): no rule reproduces Excel's answer yet, so the golden does not decide the
#                          row and the product must refuse it. Teaching the model is a deferred follow-up; the list
#                          after the counts names each row with Excel's answer.
#   The run stops if the model contradicts Excel on any such row; the counts below say how it stands to Excel.
# ANY OTHER ROW (the corpora's, and the curated groups Excel has not computed: snap-wrapped, power-squaring,
# excel-cached, gate round 9's pmt-interval and literal-untaken, and gate round 10's pmt-monotone) is decided by THE
# shared with gate B's scripts/write-proof.py; none of it the product's code; its docstring holds every rule with its
# evidence, and how far each reaches past what Excel answered), and LibreOffice (through UNO, exact
# doubles, a logical told by its LOGICAL number format) evaluates the same formula over the same inputs. The model's
#   THE SNAP: an add/sub of operands of opposite signs is 0 when |result| < 2^(e-49), e the binary exponent of its
#     LEFT operand (8 ulps of a number in the left operand's binade) - fitting all 7,747 bare root residues Excel
#     answered (requests 1 and 3, and the corpus's 6,989 cached ones; the larger operand misfits 2: cancel-ulps.00028
#     and 00042, =A-B-C over 1 and 0.5000000000000002 twice, the only rows that tell the two apart; request 4 confirms
#     it with cell operands, excel-probe-4.00044 and 00046: =A-B and =(A-B)*1 over 0.4999999999999998 and
#     the formula's BARE root add/sub (=A-B, =+A-B, the end of =0+A-B), to a defined name's body (a formula of its
#     own: =Gap*1 snaps; lookup-shapes.xlsx Sheet1!H15:H26) where the name is the formula or an operand of its root
#     operator (elsewhere a body's snap is undecided:name-snap), and to the LAST addition of EVERY SUM, root or not
#     (=SUM(A,-B)*1 is 0; excel-probe (c)); never to a root under parentheses, unary plus or minus (=(A-B), =+(A-B),
#     =-(B-A) keep 1 to 7 ulps; excel-probe (a), cancel-band), an IF branch, a SUM's other additions (=SUM(A,-B,0)
#     keeps 8.9e-16; =SUM(3,1E16,-1E16,0) is 4), or any add/sub that is not the last step (Sheet2!D1:D10).
#   THE 15-DIGIT DECIMAL ('%.14e') underlies equality and ROUND; a tie at the 16th digit goes to even: kept at an
#     even 15th digit by ROUND (Sheet2!J5, round-keeps-all.00001), taken up at an odd one by equality (compare-ulps.
#     00124: 999999999999999.5 = 1E15 is TRUE). ROUND over an odd tie, and equality over an even one, are
#     undecided:fifteen-digit-tie where the readings differ. Request 4 answered both (excel-probe-4 (t), 00034 to
#     00043): ROUND took the odd ties TOWARD zero (ROUND(1234567890123.375,2) is 1234567890123.37,
#     ROUND(100000000000001.5,0) 100000000000001), equality took the even ones AWAY from zero
#   EQUALITY: two numbers are equal when their 15-significant-digit decimals are; < and > follow (compare-ulps and
#     compare-15digit: all 119 rows where this and the 2^-48 band differ; Sheet2!F1:G10). A logical is greater than
#     every number and text, a text greater than every number, and neither equals another type; text against text is
#     case-insensitive, character by character, a trailing space counting ("a"="A", "10"<"9", "a "<>"a"); a blank
#   SUM adds left to right, a range row by row, each addition rounded, no compensation (ten 0.1 cells sum to
#     0.9999999999999999: sum-sequential.00041); it skips logicals in references, and a logical a reference gives
#   ROUND rounds x's 15-significant-digit decimal half away from zero at d places (Sheet2!J1:J8; round-large); d is
#     first rounded to 15 significant digits, then truncated toward 0 (excel-probe (h), (k)), and counts from -20 to
#     20 (round-digits) and on to 42 (one corpus cache, fuse.0c1f4102 M200OPR!U10); past them, undecided (Excel
#     observed (request 4), excel-probe-4 (v): d = 21 and 30 as the rule says; d = 100, 308, 400 leave 1234.5678 and
#     1E300 unchanged, d = -21, -30, -308, -400 give 0 for 1234.5678, and 1E300, 1E300, 0, 0 for 1E300; the model is
#   POWERS: a whole exponent by right-to-left binary exponentiation, x^-n = 1/x^n (excel-probe (p), 36 rows bit for
#     bit). A non-integer one over a positive base is sqrt(x) at 0.5, exp(b*ln x) at another b > 0 and 1/x^-b at b < 0
#     (rule power-by-exp-log): Excel's own corpus caches (exact on 5,408 where C's pow is on 36) and =2^0.5 (power.
#     00024), and Excel observed (request 4), excel-probe-4 (q): 13 more rows (b = 0.95, 1.5, 2.5, 12.5, -6.41,
#     -0.95, -1/3, -0.3, -0.5), all bit for bit, where C's pow misses 11 by 1 to 4 ulps. A negative base to b:
#     -exp(b*ln|x|) when 1/b is an odd integer (every value row bit for bit), #NUM! when 1/b is even or no integer
#     (excel-probe (e), (o)), undecided at b < 0 where the direct and reciprocal forms differ (Excel observed
#     (request 4), excel-probe-4 (r): the reciprocal -1/exp(-b*ln|x|) on all 4 such rows; the model is not yet
#   PMT: the annuity identity through log1p and expm1; any nonzero type is 1. Excel's PMT digits are not reproduced
#     bit for bit by any arrangement tried, so (gate round 9, review B4R7-V1-PMT-INEXACT) a PMT result is an
#     INTERVAL, +/- 11 units of 2^-52 of the payment's scale ((|pv*(1+r)^n| + |fv|)*|r|/|(1+r*type)*((1+r)^n-1)|, the
#     payment's own magnitude unless pv's and fv's terms cancel): 11 is Excel's largest observed miss (pmt.00065; 4 on
#     the fv-inclusive path, pmt.00077), and Excel's double lies inside the interval on all 126 Excel-observed
#     PMT-derived number rows. Calls over the same argument values are one unknown (Excel computes one double for
#     them: fv omitted is 0 and any nonzero type 1, the same double), over different ones independent; a formula is
#     evaluated at the centre and at every corner of their box, and decided only where all agree: the same logical
#     (for = and <>, also one 15-digit decimal per operand, or none shared, or the same double everywhere), the same
#     error, the same ROUND result (then exact), numbers within 1e-13 relative of each other (identical under a ROUND
#     root); its value is then the centre's. Otherwise undecided:pmt-digits (a comparison near the payment, a
#     cancellation, the 24-month amortization residue: the groups pmt and pmt-interval). The corners bound a value
#     only where it is monotone in each unknown (gate round 10, the group pmt-monotone): operands sharing an unknown
#     are decorrelated unless they are the same value (x-x is 0, x=x TRUE), x*x and an even power over a sign
#     change span 0 to the larger corner, and a pole (a divisor, a negative or zero power, PMT's nper spanning 0),
#     a truthiness test (IF's condition, PMT's type spanning 0), an exponent holding a whole number, ROUND's
#     digits over two counts and the snap's threshold stepping inside the interval are undecided:pmt-digits. A
#     dependent of a PMT cell reads it as its interval (gate B). At (1+r)^n = 1.5^100 Excel drops fv's term
#     (pmt.00065 is -0.5, 00067 -0.3333333333333333); it kept it up to 1.07^30, and past that, unless the fv-free
#     and fv-inclusive payments are within the interval's half-width (the interval then spans both, centred on the
#     fv-free one), or where (1+r)^n overflows, a payment is undecided:pmt-growth. Excel observed (request 4),
#     excel-probe-4 (s), 16 payments at rate 0.5 over 20 to 100 periods: neither the identity nor the fv-free payment
#     (off by 8 ulps to 8e-4 relative), except the fv-free -0.5 and 0 at 1.5^100; no rule reproduces them yet.
#   TEXT (en_NZ): in arithmetic and as ROUND's or PMT's argument a text converts when it is a numeral (spaces, sign,
#     point, exponent; at most 15 digits), digits grouped by commas, "$" and a numeral (each on Excel's strings and
#     its corpus caches), a whole percent with an exact hundredth, a numeral in parentheses (negative), or an H:MM
#     (AM|PM) time with an exact day fraction (each on one or two of Excel's strings, the rest by mechanism); it is
#     #VALUE! when empty or spaces, "TRUE", 0x hex, or a plain word (Excel's "abc", and 30 words in 981 corpus caches
#     of #VALUE!); anything else is undecided. Unary plus keeps a text; IF over a text is #VALUE!, but "TRUE"
#     (text-input, excel-probe (f), (m)). The model's docstring names every string each form rests on. Excel observed
#     (request 4), excel-probe-4 (w): the forms the model decides agree (25%, 6:00, $5, (5.5), 1,234,567.89 and the
#     convert, and N/A, n/a, May, a and p are #VALUE!; the model is not yet taught them.
#   A subnormal input is 0; a result below the smallest normal double is 0; x/0 and a non-finite result are errors.
# Undecided, so the product must refuse (basis undecided:<aspect>): compare-blank-logical (an ordering of a blank
#   against a logical), compare-text (texts the order rule above does not reach: punctuation, a letter against a
#   digit, an accent), if-condition-text ("FALSE" and other spellings of the logicals), text-to-number (a text no
#   form above covers), sum-parenthesised-reference and sum-text-argument (a text into SUM other than through a
#   reference), sum-reference-through-unary-plus, negative-root (1/b within 1e-9 of an integer without being one,
#   or b < 0 where -exp(b*ln|x|) and -1/exp(-b*ln|x|) differ), input-out-of-range (NaN or an infinity in a cell),
#   literal-out-of-range (a literal Excel removes on load, wherever it sits: an IF branch not taken too, the group
#   literal-untaken), round-digits (d below -20 or past 42, or a result past Excel's largest number), pmt-rate (a rate
#   at or below -1), pmt-growth and pmt-digits (above), power-algorithm (a whole exponent
#   past 1999 where squaring and pow differ, or 1/x^n over a subnormal x^n), fifteen-digit-tie (above), name-snap
#   (above), syntax (outside the grammar: a hostile row, or parentheses deeper than 250)
# Left out before any evaluation: a corpus row from a workbook with precision as displayed (calcPr
#   fullPrecision="0"; the harvest line counts them): Excel stores each result rounded to its display there (the
#   Microsoft KB "Floating-point arithmetic may give inaccurate results in Excel", on its "Precision as displayed"
#   option), so a full-precision evaluation is not what Excel caches (R2-E). A corpus row on a SHEET with Lotus
#   transition formula evaluation (sheetPr transitionEvaluation="1"; the line below lists the sheets): Excel
#   evaluates by other rules there (a text is 0 in arithmetic: such sheets' caches hold a number for 32 formulas the
#   model gives #VALUE!, and none elsewhere; gate round 8's review, R8-TFE-1), and a golden row cannot say which
#   sheet kind it is on. A row from an iterate="1" workbook stays: one evaluation over its inputs' caches is what the
# Then, for a row the model decides, by LibreOffice:
#   lo            the model and LibreOffice agree (numbers within 1e-13 relative, 0 only with 0; a row whose root is
#                 a ROUND call within 5e-16, after a named rule that reproduces LibreOffice's double exactly); a
#   error:<code>  the model and LibreOffice both give an error (LibreOffice's code): the product must refuse
#   excel:<rule>  LibreOffice is not Excel here, and the rule names why; the row holds the model's answer:
#     equal-to-15-digits     two numbers are equal when their 15-significant-digit decimals are, and order follows:
#                            Excel observed (request 3), compare-ulps and compare-15digit, all 119 rows where that and
#                            the 2^-48 band against the larger operand differ (1 = 0.9999999999999991 is FALSE, 1 =
#                            boundary); Excel observed (16.113.3, 2026-10-02), Sheet2!F1:F10 and G1:G10 (=A=B TRUE and
#                            =A>B FALSE for A = 1+k*2^-52, B = 1, k up to 16). LibreOffice's band is 2^-48 of the
#                            SMALLER operand, so 1 against 1+16 ulps is unequal there and 1 against 1-4 ulps equal, and
#                            its order follows its equality. The quirk is that band alone: a row LibreOffice decides by
#                            its other rule, two whole numbers compared exactly, is left out.
#     logical-above-every-number a logical value is never equal to a number and is greater than every number: =TRUE=1 is
#                            excel-probe (d) and (n): TRUE>1E300 and FALSE>-1, FALSE>1.5 and (1<2)>1.5 are TRUE, TRUE<0
#                            FALSE (LibreOffice compares a logical as the number 1 or 0).
#     negation-is-a-number   negating a logical value gives a number: -TRUE is -1 and --(A1>5) is 1 (LibreOffice keeps
#                            the boolean type and shows TRUE). The double-unary idiom --(condition), widely documented
#                            for SUMPRODUCT, relies on it; HANDOFF section 7 records LibreOffice's difference.
#     no-snap-before-the-last-step an add/sub that is not the formula's bare root (nor a defined name body's, nor a SUM's last
#                            addition) is never snapped to 0, not even 1 ulp from it: Excel observed (16.113.3,
#                            2026-10-02), Sheet2!D1:D10 (=(A-B)*1, A = 1+k*2^-52, B = 1, keeps every residue,
#                            2.2204460492503131E-16 at k = 1); Excel observed (request 3), excel-probe (a), (c), (i) and
#                            cancel-band: a root under parentheses, unary plus or minus (=(A-B), =+(A-B), =-(B-A)), an
#                            IF branch, =A-B+0, =SUM(A-B), a SUM's other additions (=SUM(A,-B,0) keeps 8.9e-16). Excel's
#                            own cache of enron.523276f88f H26 =(SUM(H55:H94)-H5)/H5 keeps 13 ulps inside the
#                            parentheses (gate spec R2-C). LibreOffice snaps EVERY add/sub with |a+b| < 2^-48 x
#                            min(|a|,|b|), 16 to 32 ulps, two whole numbers apart (measured: 1-(1+15 ulps) is 0 there,
#     no-snap-past-8-ulps    the formula's bare root add/sub, a defined name's body's, and every SUM's last addition are
#                            snapped to 0 only below 2^(e-49), e the binary exponent of the LEFT operand (8 ulps of a
#                            number in its binade); at or past it they keep the residue: Excel observed (16.113.3,
#                            2026-10-02), Sheet2!C7:C10 and E7:E10 (=A-B and =SUM(A,-B), A = 1+k*2^-52, B = 1, keep it
#                            for k = 8, 9, 12, 16, are 0 for k = 1, 2 and 4 to 7); Excel observed (request 3),
#                            ulps of the larger operand, under 2^-49 of the left, 0.4999999999999998, whose binade
#                            starts at 2^-2). The left-operand threshold fits all 7,747 bare root residues Excel
#                            answered (requests 1 and 3, and the corpus's 6,989 cached root add/sub residues under 16
#                            ulps); the larger operand's misfits 2. LibreOffice snaps EVERY add/sub with |a+b| < 2^-48 x
#                            min(|a|,|b|), 16 to 32 ulps, two whole numbers apart (measured: 1-(1+15 ulps) is 0 there,
#     power-by-exp-log       x^b for a non-integer b over a positive base is sqrt(x) at b = 0.5, exp(b*ln x) at any
#                            other b > 0, and 1/x^-b for b < 0 (1/sqrt(x) at -0.5). Excel's own corpus caches (gate
#                            round 7's harvest of 91,523 ^-formulas from the Excel-saved corpus): where C's pow and this
#                            rule differ, the rule is exact on 5,408 caches and pow on 36 (33 in one workbook, enron
#                            vkaminski jvcredit, calcId 92512); exp(b*ln x) on 1,845 caches in 66 workbooks at b > 0,
#                            8912.509381337457 where pow gives 8912.509381337453; the reciprocal on 2,233 caches in 38
#                            workbooks at b < 0 where the direct exp(b*ln x) differs, the direct on 2; an exponent whole
#                            only after rounding (0.98^6.000000000000001) is exp-log's in all 5 such caches where the
#                            two differ. Excel observed (request 3): power.00024 =2^0.5 and percent.00007 =2^50% are
#                            sqrt's 1.4142135623730951 (exp(0.5*ln 2) is an ulp below); Excel observed (request 4),
#                            excel-probe-4.00001 to 00013: exp(b*ln x) at b = 0.95, 1.5, 2.5, 12.5, the reciprocal at b
#                            = -6.41, -0.95, -1/3, -0.3, and 1/sqrt(x) at -0.5, all 13 bit for bit, where LibreOffice's
#                            double misses 11 by 1 to 4 ulps. LibreOffice uses C's pow.
#     power-by-squaring      x^n for a whole n is right-to-left binary exponentiation (the result multiplied by the
#                            running square for each set bit of n, low bit first, each product rounded to a double), and
#                            x^-n is 1/x^n: Excel observed (request 3), excel-probe (p), bit for bit on all 36 rows that
#                            tell pow, right-to-left and left-to-right squaring and repeated multiplication apart (n up
#                            to 1000 and down to -360, a cell or a literal exponent, ((1+r)^12-1)*100; 1/x^n, not
#                            (1/x)^n), where C's pow misses 33. Excel's own caches (gate round 7's power scan of the
#                            91,522 in-grammar formulas holding ^ in the 31,402 Excel-saved corpus workbooks) hold
#                            squaring's double in 85,900 and C's correctly rounded pow's in 57,437. Where only one of
#                            them is exact, squaring is in 28,486 (low bit first in 14,492 to 6) and pow in 23, each
#                            explained otherwise (16 by the same squaring with every product rounded twice, through the
#                            x87's 64-bit significand; 6 by sb.90e02a14e7's workbook, whose caches no evaluation of its
#                            own inputs reproduces; 1 by a non-integer power in the same formula). Past |n| = 1999, the
#                            largest the caches cover (enron.bd6ce82e5e V7, 1.027^-1999), where squaring and pow differ,
#                            and where x^n is subnormal under a reciprocal: undecided:power-algorithm. LibreOffice uses
#     round-15-digits        ROUND rounds the value's 15-significant-digit decimal (the double's 16th digit rounded, an
#                            exact tie to even), half away from zero at d places, at every position, so at or past its
#                            last digit it gives that decimal: Excel observed (16.113.3, 2026-10-02), Sheet2!J1:J8:
#                            Excel observed (request 3), round-large and round-digits: ROUND(1000000000000000.5,1) is
#                            1E15, ROUND(0.30000000000000004,16) 0.3. LibreOffice rounds the exact double instead at
#                            some positions (measured on those cells: 2, 0, 10, 1234567890123.13, 9007199254740992 and
#                            1/3 itself for J1, J2, J4, J5, J6 and J8; it agrees with Excel at J3 and J7).
#     sum-left-to-right      SUM adds left to right, a range row by row, each addition rounded: Excel's own caches hold
#                            the sequential sum, enron.eca629b535 AE51 =$AD$58-SUM($AB$58,$Z$58,...) cached
#                            6.480149750132114e-12 where the exact sum gives 6.366e-12, and =+SUM(I79:AF79)-D51-D56 in
#                            enron 66a99f4e8b and f914b63892 B80 cached -1.8189894035458565e-10 where the exact sum
#                            gives 5.09e-11 (gate spec R2-B); row by row: Excel observed (16.113.3, 2026-10-02), extras
#                            Sheet2!L9 (=SUM(P1:Q2) over P1 1E16, Q1 1, P2 -1E16 and Q2 1 is exactly 1); plainly,
#                            without compensation: Excel observed (request 3), sum-sequential.00041 =SUM(A:J) over ten
#                            0.1 is 0.9999999999999999. LibreOffice compensates its sums (measured: SUM(A1:A3) over
#                            1e16, 1, 1 is 1e16+2 there, and SUM(A1:A4) over 1e100, 1, -1e100, 1 is 2, where the
#                            sequential sums are 1e16 and 1). The quirk that explains LibreOffice's value (LoKahan)
#                            reproduces 393 of 400 random SUM shapes; a row it cannot explain is left out.
#     sum-skips-logicals     SUM ignores logical values held in a referenced cell or range (LibreOffice counts TRUE as
#                            1). Microsoft's SUM function page: "If an argument is an array or reference, only numbers
#                            in that array or reference are counted. Empty cells, logical values, or text in the array
#                            or reference are ignored." So does a logical a reference gives through parentheses or an IF
#     underflow-is-zero      a result below the smallest normal double is 0: =2^-1074 is stored as exactly 0 (Excel
#                            observed (16.113.3, 2026-10-02), Sheet2!L6), as the Microsoft KB "Floating-point arithmetic
#                            may give inaccurate results in Excel" says of underflow (LibreOffice gives #NUM!); Excel
#                            observed (request 3), excel-probe (b): a subtraction whose residue is subnormal is 0.
#     zero-power-zero        0^0 is #NUM!: Excel observed (16.113.3, 2026-10-02), Sheet2!L1 (LibreOffice gives 1). An
#                            error, so the product must refuse.
#   LibreOffice differing for any other reason leaves the row OUT (an X line)

# EXCEL'S OWN ANSWERS: 15140 curated rows (docs/review/2026-10-02-excel-request-3-results/excel-cache.jsonl 15046, docs/review/2026-10-08-excel-request-4-results/formulas/excel-cache.jsonl 94); the model against them: {'bit': 15023, 'models refuse': 59, 'tolerance': 58}

#   not bit for bit, by kind and group (the run lists every one): models refuse fifteen-digit-tie 10, models refuse negative-root 4, models refuse pmt-growth 16, models refuse round-digits 14, models refuse text-to-number 15, tolerance pmt 58

# EXCEL ANSWERED, THE MODEL REFUSES (59 rows, B5 gate round 3): each row stays a refusal (undecided:<the model's aspect>, or error:<code> where Excel gives an error) until the model is taught Excel's answer (a deferred follow-up). By the model's aspect, with Excel's answer:
# LEFT OUT, and why (the gate does not cover these; each is an X line below):
#      825  on a sheet with Lotus transition formula evaluation (sheetPr transitionEvaluation="1"): Excel evaluates by other rules there
